conviction_note: No consensus exists, so the prior-year quarter ($4.6m revenue, $(1.3)m net loss) is the only bar. The primary documents point to a revenue decline that is narrowing (the brand-partner base held near 5,200 against a 5,800 average a year ago) but still negative year on year. The headline net loss probably worsens because the tax benefit is gone (valuation allowance) and leaseback rent replaces interest. On a name that fell after 6 of its 7 prints, that gives a mild down lean (p_up 42) on a 4.5% scale. The findings sum (-0.6) and the scaled number (-0.72) agree in sign and size.
bar: Unsourced as a consensus: no analyst estimate was found for EDUC. Sized against the prior-year quarter Q2 FY26 (net revenue $4.6m, avg active Brand Partners 5,800, pre-tax loss $(1.8)m, net loss $(1.3)m, EPS $(0.15)), https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/269893/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2026-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Results. Every finding is capped small for that reason. The company gives no guidance (CEO on 2026-07-09: 'I'm certainly not forecasting what's going to be happening the rest of this year').
positioning_check: Short interest 30,705 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, about 0.4% of 8.52m shares outstanding, 1.00 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/educ/short-interest, per the sweep row read 2026-10-14). That is not a crowded short and gives no squeeze mechanism. There is no options market, so no skew. Spot is $1.31, 5.65% above the 52-week low and -20.6% from the 52-week high. The 20-day run-up is +0.77% and 20-day realised vol only 6.1%. Turnover is about 19.5k shares a day, about $25k/day. Reaction history: down after 6 of 7 prints, median |move| 3.18%, max -9.94% (Oct 2025, the same fiscal Q2).

findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 call (2026-07-09) said active PaperPie Brand Partners rose from 4,300 (end Feb) to about 5,200 after a March recruiting special and had been 'maintained ... to this day'. A Q2 FY27 average near 5,200 against 5,800 a year ago is about a -10% partner decline, against -31% in Q1 (5,300 vs 7,700) and -58% in Q2 FY26 (5,800 vs 13,900). Applying FY26's Q2/Q1 revenue-per-partner ratio (0.86) to Q1 FY27's ~$898 implies Q2 revenue of roughly $4.0-4.3m against $4.6m: still down, but the smallest year-on-year decline in two years.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-07-09) reported partners up 20% sequentially and cash up, and the stock still fell -3.18%. Q2 FY26 (2025-10-09) revenue -29% fell -9.94%. The stock has fallen after 6 of 7 prints, so improvement on this line has not been paid for.
findings.why_not_priced: The partner count is public, but nobody covers the name and no estimate converts it into a revenue number. If the narrowing decline were priced, the stock would have moved off its 52-week low area; it has been flat at $1.30 with 6% realised vol.
findings.independence: The prior-year comparison comes from a different document, the Q2 FY26 release: https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/269893/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2026-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Results. Same management source as the Q1 release (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/304633).

findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 10-Q shows the company now records no tax benefit on losses (valuation allowance: $16.5k tax expense vs a $(374)k benefit a year ago), and fixed lease cost after the Hilti leaseback rose to $388k from $171k per quarter. Q2 FY26 net loss of $(1.3)m included a $(0.46)m tax benefit. Even if pre-tax loss improves from $(1.8)m to around $(1.4)m, the headline net loss is likely about $(1.4)m, EPS about $(0.16) vs $(0.15): worse year on year at the line the wire prints. Q1 showed exactly this pattern (pre-tax loss flat, net loss $(1.40)m vs $(1.08)m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 FY27 the same tax swing made net loss and EPS worse year on year while pre-tax was flat, and the stock fell -3.18%.
findings.why_not_priced: Headline-driven retail and algo readers of a no-coverage microcap see 'net loss widens' without the tax context. Had it been priced as non-cash, the July print would not have sold off on a flat pre-tax loss.
findings.independence: The Q1 release states the tax effect (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/304633/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2027-First-Quarter-Results). It shares the company as source with the 10-Q, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: Liquidity improved and is not distressed. Q1 FY27 cash rose to $1.66m (+$0.5m) as inventory fell $1.5m to $36.2m. The company is debt-free after the $32.2m HQ sale. A $2.0m Regent Bank revolver, undrawn at 2026-05-31 and maturing 2027-03-06, exists to buy new titles. The 10-Q has no going-concern language. CFO: 'turning inventory into cash should translate into positive cash flow.'
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cash up and debt free at Q1 still met -3.18%. The Oct 2025 HQ sale did not lift the stock durably (now -20.6% from its 52-week high).
findings.why_not_priced: The market cap is about $11m against $36m of inventory, so the market is discounting inventory heavily. A second quarter of inventory-to-cash conversion would be evidence against that discount. Had it been priced, the stock would not sit near its 52-week low. Rule 4: what the money buys is new titles, and Q1 showed new-title releases; the revolver is a positive or zero, not distress.
findings.independence: The revolver is in the 8-K of 2026-03-11: https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/288147/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-New-Loan-Agreement-and-Banking-Relationship

findings.finding: Usborne concentration risk. The Q1 FY27 10-Q says Usborne may terminate on under 30 days' notice because EDC missed minimum purchases and did not provide the required letter of credit, though Usborne 'has not notified the Company of termination'. Usborne product revenue halved to $1.31m from $2.54m, Usborne purchases were $0, and Usborne refuses a disputed $1.0m FY2022 rebate. Usborne inventory is $19.6m of the $36.2m. The 10-Q filed with Q2 results will restate this, and any change in status would land in the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print carried a change in Usborne status, so there is no history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is buried in 10-Q notes, and the release and call did not mention it. The size is small because the base case is an unchanged status. Net of the rest of the company: Kane Miller, own titles and other PaperPie product are about 69% of PaperPie revenue and are unaffected, and on termination the company keeps a 12-month sell-through right.
findings.independence: The FY26 10-K carries the same language: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000031667/000118518526001927/educ10k022826.htm. Same issuer, so not independent.

findings.finding: Peer read for the identical quarter (June-August 2026): Scholastic reported Q1 FY27 on 2026-09-24 with revenue -4% to $216.8m, citing lower Children's Book Publishing and Distribution and Education revenue under school-budget pressure. The stock fell 12.2% after hours. This is a weak children's-book demand backdrop for EDUC's summer quarter, which also serves schools through its Publishing segment (-40% in Q1).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior evidence that EDUC trades on peer prints.
findings.why_not_priced: EDUC is thinly traded and nobody maps peer prints onto it, so the stock has not moved since Scholastic reported (20-day run-up +0.77%). This is a proxy: Scholastic sells through book fairs and trade, EDUC through an MLM channel, so transmission is unconfirmed and the size is small.
findings.independence: Proxy; separate source from the EDUC documents. Coverage of the reaction: https://www.rttnews.com/story.aspx?Id=3693885

outside_window.finding: The $2.0m Regent revolver matures 2027-03-06 and needs renewal; the CEO is a guarantor.

baseline_tension: No skew and a flat run-up, so the only market statement is the reaction history: the stock has sold off after 6 of 7 prints. The mild negative lean agrees with that history; the narrowing partner decline is the one item that cuts against it.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sells its prints): partner-trend finding +0.5 -> +0.3
Rule 2 (one-off below operating income): the tax-allowance/net-loss finding was relabelled one_off and cut -0.8 -> -0.5
Rule 9 (size a segment net of the rest): Usborne termination-risk finding -0.5 -> -0.3, net of the ~69% non-Usborne PaperPie revenue and the 12-month sell-through right
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the revolver funds new titles, so the financing finding stays at +0.2
Rule 6 (bar unsourced): all findings were already small; caps kept
Rule 8 (thin name): abs_move_pct 4.0 -> 4.5; p_up unchanged at 42
